newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SanMig down on lower net prospect.
newsitem.headline: SanMig down on lower net prospect.

text.p: Food and beer firm San Miguel Corp slipped by midsession as prospects of weak second quarter earnings turned off investors, brokers said.
"Income for the second quarter is expected to be weak due to lower sales volume," Astro del Castillo, an analyst at A&A Securities, said.
San Miguel A shares fell 2.50 pesos, or 6.58 percent, to 35.50 pesos, while its B shares which are open to foreigners fell 3.50 pesos, or 5.56 percent, to 59.50.
A recent Reuters survey showed that investment houses were expecting a 0.41 percent decline in its first half earnings.
Investors were shifting to cheaper stocks. "There are more shares which have better valuation than San Miguel," del Castillo added.

Aside from the expected income slowdown, San Miguel is currently embroiled in a controversy with rival Asia Brewery Inc (ABI) which has filed a 112 million peso damage suit against San Miguel for allegedly hoarding ABI's empty bottles.
San Miguel said the empty ABI bottles were accumulated in late 1980s when it had a bottle swap agreement with ABI, a deal which was terminated by ABI after some months.
Brokers, however, said the fears of lower income were causing more concern than the legal tussle with ABI.
